message.content:
In the repo at /bench/repo, I need to answer: What background workers/runners does the server actually START at runtime, and what drives each one's scheduling (e.g., setInterval, cron library, job queue, event-driven)? Also determine whether any scheduling infrastructure exists in the codebase (e.g., a cron/scheduler module, job queue implementation) that is NOT actually used/started by the server.

Search breadth: very thorough.

Steps:
1. Find the server entry point(s) (e.g., server/ directory, main.ts, index.ts, app startup).
2. Trace what background workers/runners/pollers/schedulers are instantiated and started at server boot (look for names like worker, runner, poller, scheduler, cron, queue, interval, daemon, heartbeat, cleanup, sweeper).
3. For each started worker, identify the exact mechanism driving its scheduling: setInterval/setTimeout loop, cron expression via a library (node-cron, croner, bullmq repeatable, etc.), database polling, event subscription, etc. Cite file paths and line numbers.
4. Search for any scheduling/cron/queue infrastructure defined in the codebase that is never wired into server startup (dead/unused code). Verify by checking imports/references.

Return: a list of each runner actually started by the server with (file path:line, trigger mechanism, interval/schedule if any), plus any unused scheduling infrastructure with evidence it's unused (file path, and confirmation nothing imports/starts it).

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

content.text:
This is the **memos** Go project (not Node) — a single binary, entry point `cmd/memos/main.go` → `server.NewServer` / `server.Start`. No cron/job-queue library exists in `go.mod`; everything is hand-rolled with `time.Ticker`, `init()` goroutine pools, and channels.

## Runners actually started by the server

**1. S3 presign runner — the only thing in `startBackgroundRunners`**
- `/bench/repo/server/server.go:153-174` (`startBackgroundRunners`, called from `Start` at `/bench/repo/server/server.go:129`)
- `/bench/repo/server/server.go:163` — `s3presignRunner.RunOnce(ctx)` runs **synchronously on the boot path** (blocks server startup for a full paged scan of all S3 attachments).
- `/bench/repo/server/server.go:167-171` — goroutine running `Run(s3Context)`.
- Mechanism: `time.NewTicker` at `/bench/repo/server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:30`, interval `runnerInterval = time.Hour * 12` at `/bench/repo/server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27`. Each tick pages `ListAttachments` in batches of 100 and re-presigns URLs older than 4 days.
- Shutdown: cancel func stored at `server.go:159`, cancelled in `stopBackgroundRunners` (`server.go:176`), waited on via `backgroundRunnerWG` (`server.go:184`).

**2. Store cache cleanup loops (×3) — started by `store.New`, not by the server**
- `/bench/repo/store/cache/cache.go:83` — `go c.cleanupLoop()` inside `cache.New`.
- Mechanism: `time.NewTicker(c.config.CleanupInterval)` at `/bench/repo/store/cache/cache.go:201`; interval is `5 * time.Minute`, set at `/bench/repo/store/store.go:41`.
- Three instances are created at `/bench/repo/store/store.go:51-53` (`instanceSettingCache`, `userCache`, `userSettingCache`) — reached from `/bench/repo/cmd/memos/main.go:64`. Stopped in `Store.Close` (`/bench/repo/store/store.go:71-74`), which the server calls at `server.go:146`.

**3. Webhook async dispatch pool — package `init()`, event-driven queue**
- `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:42-55` — `init()` spawns **4 worker goroutines** ranging over `asyncPostQueue`, a buffered channel of cap 128 declared at `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:39`.
- No timer at all — purely event-driven; producers call `PostAsync` (`/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:184`) from `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go:43` and `:71`.
- Started implicitly by import (`/bench/repo/cmd/memos/main.go:18`). These goroutines are never stopped on shutdown.

**4. Email async sender pool — package `init()`, event-driven queue**
- `/bench/repo/internal/email/email.go:16-36` — `init()` spawns **2 worker goroutines** over `asyncEmailQueue` (cap 128, `/bench/repo/internal/email/email.go:14`).
- Event-driven; producer is `email.SendAsync`, wired at `/bench/repo/server/notification/email.go:30`. Also never stopped on shutdown.

**5. HTTP serve goroutine** — `/bench/repo/server/server.go:124` (`httpServer.Serve(listener)`), plus the shutdown-wait goroutine at `/bench/repo/server/server.go:186` and the signal handler at `/bench/repo/cmd/memos/main.go:99`. Not "workers," but they are the boot-time goroutines.

**Per-request goroutines/tickers (not boot-started, listed for completeness)**
- SSE heartbeat: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/sse_handler.go:64` — one `time.NewTicker` per connection, `sseHeartbeatInterval = 30 * time.Second` (`sse_handler.go:17`).
- SSE fan-out is push/event-driven, no poller: `SSEHub.Broadcast` at `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go:115` with per-client 32-buffer channels (`sse_hub.go:74`), dropping on full buffer.
- PAT last-used write: fire-and-forget goroutine per authenticated PAT request at `/bench/repo/server/auth/authenticator.go:179-185`, using `context.Background()` (survives request cancellation, unbounded fan-out).

## Scheduling infrastructure that is NOT used

**A. `internal/scheduler` — an entire cron scheduler package, completely dead**

Non-test files: `/bench/repo/internal/scheduler/scheduler.go`, `job.go`, `parser.go`, `middleware.go`, `doc.go` (~640 LOC of production code, ~830 LOC of tests).

It is a full GitHub-Actions-style cron engine: hand-written 5- and 6-field cron expression parser (`/bench/repo/internal/scheduler/parser.go:30`, `ParseCronExpression`), timezone-aware job execution, middleware chain with `Recovery`/`Logging`/`Timeout` (`/bench/repo/internal/scheduler/middleware.go:27,51,74`), and graceful `Stop` (`/bench/repo/internal/scheduler/scheduler.go:169`). Its driving mechanism is one goroutine per job (`/bench/repo/internal/scheduler/scheduler.go:113`) computing `schedule.Next(now)` and sleeping on a `time.NewTimer` (`/bench/repo/internal/scheduler/scheduler.go:145`).

Evidence it is unused: the only importers of `github.com/usememos/memos/internal/scheduler` in the whole repo are its own tests —
- `/bench/repo/internal/scheduler/example_test.go:10`
- `/bench/repo/internal/scheduler/integration_test.go:13`

Nothing in `cmd/`, `server/`, or `store/` imports it, and `scheduler.New(...)` / `.Register(...)` / `.Start()` appear nowhere outside those two test files. Note `/bench/repo/AGENTS.md:69` advertises `internal/` as containing "scheduler, cron", which is documentation for infrastructure that has no production call site.

**B. `memopayload.Runner` — dead runner type inside a live package**

`/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:14-72` defines `Runner`, `NewRunner`, and `(*Runner).RunOnce` (a batched rebuild of every memo's payload). A repo-wide grep for `memopayload.NewRunner` and `memopayload.Runner` returns **zero hits**, including tests. The package is imported (`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:18`) only for the free function `RebuildMemoPayload` (`/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:74`), called synchronously inline at `memo_service.go:108` and `memo_service.go:447`. So the directory `server/runner/memopayload` is named like a background runner but contains no running runner.

**C. No third-party scheduling deps** — `go.mod` has no `robfig/cron`, `go-co-op/gocron`, `asynq`, `river`, or any job-queue library; the only "queues" are the two unbounded-consumer channel pools in §3 and §4.

## Net picture

Exactly **one** conceptual periodic job is wired up by `Server.startBackgroundRunners`: the 12-hour S3 presign refresh (`server/server.go:162` → `s3presign/runner.go:27`). Three 5-minute cache sweepers ride along via `store.New`. Two `init()`-time channel worker pools (webhook ×4, email ×2) handle event-driven async work and are never shut down. Meanwhile a complete, well-tested cron scheduler sits in `internal/scheduler` with no production caller, and a batch memo-payload runner sits in `server/runner/memopayload` with no caller either.
